about: Saltbound - people's lines (FH2, D81). Read by USaltTalkSubsystem (World/SaltTalk.cpp) at the start of play; sb.Talk.Reload reads it again.
speakers: who speaks. name (shown in small capitals on the sheet), seal (the wax mark's glyph: Anchor, Wave, Island), point (the hub point
that stands for them until they have an actor of their own), entries (the first whose conditions hold is the line they open with).
lines: id -> text, do (actions when the line is shown), choices (up to three numbered answers 1-3 and one plain answer E, each with
next: the line it leads to, or empty to end the talk; if: conditions), next (for a line without choices: where E goes; empty ends).
calls: lines called in passing on the small scrap beside the speaker (idea B): on (a beat that starts it), near (cm, how close the
player must be), seconds (how long it shows; 0 = by its length).
Conditions: beat:X, tool:X, item:X (in the satchel), tear (the boat's sail is torn), night, day:N (day N or later); ! in front negates.
Actions: beat:X (records a story beat), tool:X (gives a tool), item:X:N (puts N of X into the satchel).

keeper.first.speaker: Keeper
keeper.first.text: “Another one from the Gale. Nobody leaves; you get used to it. That old boat at the pier was the Cartographer’s. Make her sail and she’s yours.”

choices.text: I carry a letter. The sea got into it.

keeper.letter.wet.speaker: Keeper
keeper.letter.wet.text: “Then dry it before it falls apart. The fire pit up the path: the embers never quite go out. Bring it back when it can be read.”

keeper.letter.wet.again.speaker: Keeper
keeper.letter.wet.again.text: “Still soaked? The fire pit up the path. Hold it close to the embers, not in them.”

keeper.letter.speaker: Keeper
keeper.letter.text: “Let me see that. … Rowan. Nobody has said that name here in seven years. That’s the Cartographer’s own name, and Wren is the one they talked about every night at this counter. So you came in after them.”

keeper.south.speaker: Keeper
keeper.south.text: “South. Into the storm, where the sky stays black at noon. The sea won’t let a boat through there. But they left a trail: their camp on the little islet past the Spire. They watched the storm from there for a year before they went.”

keeper.who.speaker: Keeper
keeper.who.text: “A castaway like you, years back. Best hand with a chart this sea has seen, and never stopped wanting to go home. Seven years ago they sailed south into the storm and didn’t come back. Left me the boat to mind.”

keeper.sail.speaker: Keeper
keeper.sail.text: “Then mend it. The Cartographer never trusted a store: half of what they owned is buried somewhere. Spare canvas too, I’d wager.”

keeper.gift.speaker: Keeper
keeper.gift.text: “Take my shovel, and a lantern; the nights are long here. They swore by the leaning palm on this beach: ‘three paces seaward and dig’. Their chest is still aboard, if you want their own word for it.”

keeper.cache.speaker: Keeper
keeper.cache.text: “The leaning palm, three paces seaward. The Cartographer buried things the way other folk bury grudges: deep, and close to home.”

choices.text: I carry a letter. The sea got into it.

keeper.who.again.speaker: Keeper
keeper.who.again.text: “A castaway like you, years back, who never stopped wanting to go home. Seven years ago they sailed south into the storm and didn’t come back.”

keeper.mend.speaker: Keeper
keeper.mend.text: “Sailcloth? Then sit at the mast’s foot and sew. A tear like that takes two patches; don’t skimp on the second.”

choices.text: I carry a letter. The sea got into it.

keeper.ready.speaker: Keeper
keeper.ready.text: “She’ll sail. Take her round the lagoon first, and mind the reef by the Spire: she doesn’t like rocks.”

choices.text: I carry a letter. The sea got into it.

keeper.spire.speaker: Keeper
keeper.spire.text: “The stack to the north-north-east with the broken tower on it. Older than anyone’s grandmother. Some nights there’s a light up there, and nobody to light it.”

keeper.light.speaker: Keeper
keeper.light.text: “Still here? The light was burning on the Spire again last night. The Cartographer used to watch it from this beach.”

keeper.idle.speaker: Keeper
keeper.idle.text: “The tide waits for nobody. Good day for it, whatever it is.”

keeper.castoff.speaker: Keeper
keeper.castoff.text: “Mind the reef by the Spire. She doesn’t like rocks.”
